title: Adaptive Kernel Prober and Clock Harmonizer for MIG and H100/L40S/A10
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We will implement a lightweight adaptive kernel prober combined with a clock harmonization controller that constrains probing overhead while improving kernel selection accuracy across H100, L40S, and A10 devices and mixed MIG partitions. This ticket covers the runtime changes to: 1) probe candidate microkernels at low-cost sampling rates, 2) tie probe results to SKU+MIG metadata and active sequence-length histograms, and 3) apply temporary clock steering guidance when probes show a clear perf delta for a given kernel bundle. The goal is to reduce median prefill latency variance and tail decode latency without increasing steady-state token cost beyond 3%.
Context:
We've seen cases where static kernel ranking misroutes workloads on mixed MIG fleets and across H100/L40S/A10 families, especially for short-prefill chat workloads and bursty inference that escalates clocks. Prior kernel-probing attempts were either too expensive (full exhaustive probes) or too coarse (per-sku static heuristics). This design introduces a middle-ground: short probabilistic probes, combined with a brief, safe clock harmonization window to reveal kernel-level differences that only appear under specific GPU frequency bands.
Scope:
- Implement probe dispatcher and scoring in the runtime kernel manager.
- Integrate SKU+MIG metadata tagging into the kernel cache.
- Implement a clock harmonization policy that recommends temporary clock increases (bounded by per-SKU safe deltas) during probes and yields immediately after.
acceptance_criteria: Probing adds <1.5ms median overhead per affected request at 95th percentile load
Median prefill latency improvement >=6% for short-prefill workloads on mixed-MIG fleets
95th percentile decode latency improvement >=4% on L40S for the targeted kernels
Steady-state token cost increase <=3% measured over 24h A/B run
No SLO violations introduced during probes (observability dashboard and alerts validated)
timeline: 2025-02-20: Ticket created and scoped by Aisha. Initial perf hypothesis logged.
2025-02-24: Small bench harness created to run controlled probes on H100/L40S/A10 in lab. Connor and Mei ran first 500-sample sweep.
2025-02-27: Bench results show 7-12% perf delta for K1 vs K2 under +10% clock on L40S for 128-token prefill. Decided to add bounded clock harmonization to reveal deltas safely.
2025-03-01: Prototype probe dispatcher merged to feature branch (pr: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2124). Lightweight sampling rate introduced (1% of requests by default).
2025-03-03: Telemetry schema extended (pr: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/879) to tag kernel_probe=true and include pre-probe clocks and post-probe clocks.
2025-03-05: Begin small staging canary against dedicated cluster group 'ded-l40s-canary-1'. Observed no errors; initial tail latency decreased 3% in canary.
comments: Connor R (2025-02-25): Bench run suggests K2 outperforms K1 for 64-256 token prefill on L40S at boosted clocks. Need to confirm on A10 and H100 under MIG split.
Mei Zhang (2025-02-27): Added MIG mapping table to lab inventory; A10 exhibits different sensitivity to clock bumps — limited to +5% safe delta.
James O'Neill (runtime lead) (2025-03-02): Make sure probes have an escape hatch — controller to back off sampling if error rate or power draw spikes beyond thresholds.
Connor R (2025-03-04): Canary run: kernel routing flip caused small 1.2% cost bump but reduced prefill p50 by 9ms. Need to quantify across 24h.
steps: Design: finalize probe sampling and scoring algorithm (Aisha)
Runtime: implement probe dispatcher and kernel cache tagging (Connor)
Safety: add clock harmonization limits per SKU and a global emergency-backoff (James)
Telemetry: record before/after clocks, kernel_id, probe_outcome, and energy metrics (Mei)
Staging: run canary on dedicated cluster group for 72 hours and validate metrics (Ops)
Rollout: gradual rollout to 10% of traffic with automatic rollback on SLO breaches
decision_log: 2025-02-26: Chosen probabilistic sampling (1%) over deterministic per-epoch probing to limit overhead.
2025-02-27: Add temporary clock harmonization during probes with per-SKU caps: H100:+8%, L40S:+10%, A10:+5%.
2025-03-01: Telemetry tagging required for all probe events and MUST be sampled into 100% logs for first 72h of any canary.
2025-03-03: If probe-related error rate >0.1% or GPU power draw delta >12W, immediately disable probes for that host and alert oncall.
